newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen stays buoyant in wake of weak stocks.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen stays buoyant in wake of weak stocks.

text.p: The recent rise in SIMEX Euroyen futures cooled slightly on Friday after a feeble rebound in Tokyo stock prices, but dealers said the market remained buoyant
"The rally fizzled out after Tokyo stocks bounced, but it still has some way to go higher," a dealer with a foreign bank said, noting the outlook for the Tokyo share market was gloomy.
A Japanese holiday next Monday also contributed to sapping liquidity, some dealers said.
June Euroyen futures was quoted at 99.42 at 1115 GMT against its previous settlement on the IMM at 99.40. September was pegged at 99.32 against a previous settlement of 99.30.
The market's topside was seen possibly another five to six ticks higher, underpinned by the Bank of Japan's tendency to maintain interest rates at currently weak levels.
The 225-share Nikkei average closed up 119.79 points today at 19,690.46, but see-sawed indecisively between losses and gains.
Trade on Eurodollar futures was light except for the morning session where several major houses were active buyers.
Forward contracts were especially supported by overnight strength in U.S. treasuries after U.S. domestic data pushed T-bond yields to their lowest levels this week.
March Eurodollars ended unchanged against their IMM close at 94.45, while June closed at 94.34, compared with 94.32.
In Japanese government bond futures, prices drifted off from intraday highs and closed fractionally up, at 126.15 for March, with the weak Japanese stock market outlook weighing on prices.
Trade consisted mainly of position adjustments ahead of the Monday Tokyo holiday and year-end closings.
A volume of 390 lots traded for the key March contract.
